items.title: Product of the Day — Wearable Pizza
items.text:
The Wearable Pizza is a fully functional, edible pizzeria integrated into a wearable garment. Made from a specially developed stretchy dough material, users can enjoy their favorite toppings while moving freely around town. The pizza's sauce-based adhesive ensures a secure fit during even the most vigorous activities.

As hunger strikes, simply rip open the pie-top zipper to reveal a steaming hot meal. And when finished, don't worry – the crumbs will magically compost into nutrient-rich fertilizer, leaving behind only satisfied satisfaction and perhaps a faint scent of oregano wafting through the air.

Categories: food

items.title: On This Day — October 23
items.text:
• 4004 BC – James Ussher's calculated First day of the world based on the Old Testament. Creation, he believed, occurred at what would have been nightfall on the previous day.
• 42 BC – Liberators' civil war: Mark Antony and Octavian decisively defeat an army under Brutus in the second part of the Battle of Philippi, with Brutus committing suicide and ending the civil war.
• 425 – Valentinian III is elevated as Roman emperor at the age of six.
• 502 – The Synodus Palmaris, called by Gothic king Theoderic, absolves Pope Symmachus of all charges, thus ending the schism of Antipope Laurentius.
• 1086 – Spanish Reconquista: At the Battle of Sagrajas, the Almoravids defeat the Castilians, but are unable to take advantage of their victory.
